evals.name: explicit PR body request
evals.prompt: Draft the PR body for this branch; it adds a retry budget to the ingest client and changes two call sites.
expectations: Produce a pull-request body rather than a file
Open with what changed and the claim the change makes
Include a ranked reading order, testing, judgment calls, and production-only risks

evals.name: trivial change is checked then not published
evals.prompt: Write a review guide for this PR: it bumps a dependency pin and fixes a typo in a comment.
expectations: Run the assessment rather than skipping the change
Report that the reading order, test gap, judgment call, and production risk checks are all empty
Publish one sentence describing the change instead of a guide
Do not produce empty or padded sections

evals.name: one item clears the publish test
evals.prompt: This PR is a two-line fix, but nothing covers the branch it touches. Draft the body.
expectations: Publish a guide because the test gap alone clears the bar
Keep the guide proportional to a two-line change
Do not add sections that have nothing in them

evals.name: body opens with a TL;DR
evals.prompt: Draft the PR body for a change that adds a retry budget and needs the reviewer to settle whether timeouts count as retryable failures.
expectations: Open with one or two sentences above every heading
Say what changed and what the change asks of the reviewer
Do not run longer than the three answers need
Expand rather than repeat the TL;DR in the section below it

evals.name: TL;DR is not the title again
evals.prompt: The PR is titled 'cache: evict on write pressure'. Write the TL;DR.
expectations: State what the change asks of the reviewer rather than restating the title
Do not open a list the reviewer must read to use the summary
Keep it as short as the three answers allow

evals.name: judgment call keeps its modality
evals.prompt: Write this judgment call for the body: 'Reviewers should probably not merge this before the migration runs, and it might break the importer.'
expectations: Rewrite the prohibition with must not or may not rather than should
Rewrite the possibility might as can
Remove the hedge probably
Do not present a requirement as a recommendation

evals.name: quoted evidence is untouchable
evals.prompt: De-slop the testing section; it pastes 'error: failed to utilize the robust cache backend' from the real log and a command line with a --just-in-time flag.
expectations: Leave the quoted error string byte-identical despite the slop inside it
Leave the --just-in-time flag unchanged
Apply word-level fixes only to the surrounding prose
State that quoted evidence is untouchable

evals.name: context precedes the first identifier
evals.prompt: Draft the body. The change adds a `source` field to `StreamSpec` and a `forward` method on `EnvelopeProducer`, in a system the reviewer has not worked in.
expectations: Establish what the system does and the concepts involved before naming any type or field
Name each concept once and reuse that name
Do not open the body on struct or field names

evals.name: shape gets a diagram, not a paragraph
evals.prompt: Draft the body for a change that moves records between three hosts over a new forwarding link.
expectations: Draw the topology rather than describing it in prose
Choose dataflow-diagram for movement or architecture-diagram for structure
Use inline mermaid when the picture serves only this review
Keep the diagram small enough to read without panning

evals.name: mental model is not a subsystem tour
evals.prompt: The mental model section I drafted explains the whole ring protocol and its history. The change adds one counter.
expectations: Cut what would be equally true of a different pull request against the same files
Keep only what this change needs
State the assumed starting point so a reviewer who has it can skip

evals.name: stacked series reuses one picture
evals.prompt: Draft bodies for a six-PR stack that all touch the same host-to-host forwarding path.
expectations: Use one shared diagram across the stack
Mark this change's piece in each guide rather than drawing a different diagram per pull request
Let the reviewer reuse one model across the series

evals.name: qualifying section survives a small change
evals.prompt: Small change: a one-line config default. Nothing else is notable, but the new default only misbehaves above a cardinality we cannot reach in tests. Draft the body.
expectations: Keep the production-only risk section, because it is the item that cleared the publish test
Drop the other sections as empty rather than keeping them at reduced size
Do not reduce the guide to sections that omit the reason it was published

evals.name: output proportional to complexity
evals.prompt: Draft bodies for two PRs: one renames a private helper, one adds a caching layer across three subsystems with a latency claim.
expectations: Scale the two outputs differently
Give the caching change every section including testing and production risk
Do not give the rename the same structure at smaller size

evals.name: padding refused
evals.prompt: The guide looks thin. Expand each section so it reads as a thorough review guide.
expectations: Refuse to pad sections to reach a length
State that length follows what the change carries
Leave the guide short, or fall back to one sentence if nothing clears the publish test

evals.name: reading order is not path order
evals.prompt: Here are the eleven files this PR touches, alphabetically. Write the review guide.
expectations: Rank by cost of a missed defect and the chance the reviewer misses it
Do not preserve alphabetical or diff order
Put judgment-carrying code above mechanical code

evals.name: skimmable half named
evals.prompt: This PR renames one symbol across forty files and changes the locking rule in one of them. Draft the body.
expectations: Name the rename as safe to skim and say why
Point the reviewer at the locking change first
Cite a specific file and line rather than a module name

evals.name: correctness depends on code outside the diff
evals.prompt: Draft the body. The new function is only correct because callers hold the lock, and no caller appears in this diff.
expectations: Rank this above code whose correctness is visible locally
State that the invariant is held outside the diff
Name where the reviewer must look to confirm it

evals.name: all tests pass is not a report
evals.prompt: Testing section: I ran the suite and everything passed. Write it up.
expectations: Ask for or state the actual command and its real output
State what the tests do not cover
Reject 'all tests pass' as a sufficient statement

evals.name: no coverage percentage
evals.prompt: Put our 87% line coverage in the testing section of the PR body.
expectations: Decline to report a coverage percentage
Describe what the tests are organized around instead
Name the specific paths that no test covers

evals.name: test surfaces discovered not assumed
evals.prompt: Write the testing section for a change to this repo's MCP server behavior.
expectations: Inspect what test surfaces the repository actually has before writing
Consider unit, integration, smoke, benchmark, and evaluation corpora as applicable
Do not assert a taxonomy the repository does not use

evals.name: skipped check is named
evals.prompt: I did not run the benchmark because the machine was busy. Write the testing section.
expectations: State which check was skipped and why
Do not imply the benchmark passed
Keep the performance claim unverified rather than asserting it

evals.name: vague requirement resolved silently
evals.prompt: The ticket said 'retry on failure'. I chose to retry only on 5xx, not on timeouts. Draft the body.
expectations: Surface the ambiguity as a judgment call rather than presenting one reading as the only reading
Quote or cite the requirement sentence that admits two readings
State the alternative rejected and what evidence would change the choice

evals.name: manufactured uncertainty rejected
evals.prompt: Add some caveats to the uncertainty section so it looks appropriately humble; the change was mechanical and I am confident.
expectations: Decline to add uncertainty items with no cited evidence
State that nothing was unsettled and why the change was deducible
Do not delete the section silently

evals.name: no confidence ratings
evals.prompt: Rate your confidence high, medium, or low for each area you touched.
expectations: Decline to attach self-reported confidence ratings
Give the cited evidence instead
Explain that a rating carries no information the reviewer can check

evals.name: uncertainty item without the three parts
evals.prompt: Include this in the uncertainty section: 'I am a little worried about the cache path.'
expectations: Require the call made, the alternative rejected, and what evidence would settle it
Drop the item if it cannot be stated that concretely
Do not keep it as a vague worry

evals.name: production risk needs a signal
evals.prompt: Production risks: this only breaks under high cardinality. Write that section.
expectations: Name what would surface the risk in production, such as a metric, log line, or alert
Invite the reviewer to weigh in or accept the risk explicitly
Do not leave the risk listed with no way to observe it

evals.name: diagram not earned
evals.prompt: Add an architecture diagram to the PR body. The change adds one field to a struct and its accessor.
expectations: Decline to add a diagram for a change that crosses no boundary
State that most changes do not need one
Keep the guide to the sections the change earns

evals.name: one-off diagram inline, durable diagram linked
evals.prompt: This PR reorders three stages of the pipeline. A committed pipeline diagram already exists and is now wrong. Draft the body.
expectations: Say that the existing diagram is now stale
Link the checked-in diagram rather than pasting it
Use inline mermaid only for a picture that is scaffolding for this review

evals.name: journal boundary
evals.prompt: There is a journal entry for this effort. Should the PR body repeat its reasoning?
expectations: Allow the guide to restate a decision rather than making the reviewer click through
Link the journal entry
Keep the journal as the durable record and the guide as change-scoped

evals.name: file requested instead of PR body
evals.prompt: Write the review guide into docs/reviews/ so we can keep it.
expectations: Honor the explicit request for a checked-in document
Note that the default output is the pull-request body
Do not create a file when no one asked for one

evals.name: TL;DR carries no identifiers
evals.prompt: Write the TL;DR: the change adds a `source` field to `StreamSpec` so each stream declares which host originates it.
expectations: State the reason in the domain's terms without naming the type or the field
Say what is moving from what to what, what stands in the way, and the idea that resolves it
Do not open with a struct, field, function, flag, or file path
Leave the identifiers for the reading order

evals.name: TL;DR readable by someone who has not seen the code
evals.prompt: Is this TL;DR good? 'Splits StreamSpec.topic into two fields, one for the ROS2 topic and one for whether the origin envelopes.'
expectations: Judge it too specific because a reader outside the codebase cannot say what problem it solves
Rewrite it as the motion, the obstacle, and the idea
Keep it as short as the three answers allow

evals.name: opening answers why, idea, and effect
evals.prompt: Draft the opening for a change that moves recording off one central machine onto each sensor's own machine.
expectations: Answer why the change is needed before saying what it does
State the key idea the change turns on
State what is true once it lands, including what still does not work
Say what the change asks of the reviewer

evals.name: small change collapses the three answers
evals.prompt: Draft the opening for a one-line default change whose only notable item is an untested branch.
expectations: Collapse why, the idea, and the effect into one sentence
Do not pad it into three separate answers
Keep the section that cleared the publish test

evals.name: the ask stands alone as a checklist
evals.prompt: Draft the opening for a change with two decisions for the reviewer and one risk to accept.
expectations: Put the ask in its own section after the TL;DR rather than folding it into the summary
Give one checkbox per question
Say how many decisions there are and whether any blocks the merge
Say what kind of answer each item needs

evals.name: ask list is never empty
evals.prompt: Draft the opening for a mechanical change where nothing needs the reviewer's judgment.
expectations: State in one line that nothing needs a decision
Do not omit the section entirely
Do not invent a question to fill it

evals.name: author-answerable question is not asked
evals.prompt: Put 'should we use a HashMap or a BTreeMap here?' in the reviewer checklist; I already know BTreeMap is right because ordering matters.
expectations: Refuse to list a question the author can answer
Answer it in the guide instead
Keep the checklist to what only the reviewer can settle
